policy: Begin a left-input hold once when remaining runway arc first crosses the threshold. Hold for the stated number of simulation ticks, including any intervening flight. Then release to right input and never re-trigger the brake. One explicit initial jump seed; carried state afterward.
interpretation: At this one seed, finite brake release avoids the timeouts found with the previous continuously re-evaluated threshold policy. This supports testing ordinary release/recovery before diagnosing a geometry trap. All twelve late-threshold-80 cases take the collector, but some earlier-threshold route outcomes differ between Forgiving and Precision. Do not collapse the two modes or infer a universal timing window.
negative_comparison: A local exploratory equality comparison across grip modes failed: their complete trajectories and some receiver outcomes are not identical. No cross-mode equivalence is claimed or required of the product.
next_native_gate: Test from the actual preview start with ordinary controls: no-brake upper route, intended lower route, early brake/release, no-input coast and useful road recovery. Show the decision before it is needed, avoid relying on a last-instant reaction cue, and preserve all accepted deliveries and traversal cases.
limitations: A single seeded approach, not native spawn
No complete terrain, enemy, packet or swept-body/deck qualification
No controller hardware, human timing, enjoyment or performance observations
This is an experiment, not a new automatic brake or shipped chapter fork
